summary: Weekly POC check-in to review quality evaluation results from last week's prompt set changes; discussed a small regression on clinical note summarization for short notes, tradeoffs between applying guardrails vs tuning prompts, and next steps to run a 3k-sample regression on quantized variant. Action items assigned and timeline agreed for next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're at 15:00 UTC, should we do quick intros?
[00:07] Sara (Meadowline): Hi, Sara here — Head of ML.
[00:09] Tom (Meadowline): Tom, CTO.
[00:11] Maya (Meadowline): Maya, data sci.
[00:14] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood, focusing on model tuning and evals.
[00:16] Alex (Redwood CSM): Alex, CSM.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool. Quick agenda — walk through last week's eval, highlight regressions, discuss guardrails, decide next steps. Sound good?
[00:24] Tom: Sounds good.
[00:26] Jordan: Okay, Priya you want to kick off with the results?
[00:28] Priya: Yeah, sure. So we ran the updated prompt set you sent Monday against the dev suite — 1,200 samples total across clinical summarization, coding hints, and triage classification. Overall macro-accuracy improved about 3% on the triage set but we did observe a regression on short clinical note summarization — average Rouge-L dropped ~4 points for notes under 80 tokens.
[00:48] Maya: Hmm, that's the subset we care about for quick discharge notes. Do you see pattern on hallucinations?
[00:54] Priya: Good question. Hallucinations didn't spike overall, but for those short notes we saw more truncation and occasionally missing medication mentions. It looks like the new prompt framing that reduces verbosity is over-constraining for short inputs.
[01:09] Jordan: Right — the prompt that encouraged concision trimmed out details. That's a typical tradeoff, latency and brevity vs fidelity.
[01:16] Sara: Can you show an example?
[01:18] Priya: Sure. Example A: original note — "Patient reports mild chest pain, on lisinopril 10mg." Golden summary: "Mild chest pain; on lisinopril 10mg." Model with new prompt: "Mild chest pain." — dropped medication.
[01:33] Maya: That's concerning. Medication is critical.
[01:35] Priya: Agreed. We also compared the quantized variant q4_0 that you asked about — the q4_0 variant had similar pattern but slightly worse recall on entities by ~2 points. So still an issue but not catastrophic.
[01:49] Tom: So is this a prompt fix or we need to bump model or disable quantization for this path?
[01:55] Priya: There are three levers: 1) revert the concision guardrail for short notes or make it conditional, 2) add explicit entity-preservation instructions in the prompt ("always include meds, allergies"), 3) run the non-quantized variant for short notes. Each has cost/perf tradeoffs.
[02:11] Jordan: We should weigh latency. Non-quantized will increase cost and latency — do we have numbers?
[02:16] Priya: For the full throughput tests, non-quantized raised token latency ~12% and cost per 1k tokens ~1.8x. But if you route only short-note path to full precision, the overall impact is small.
[02:28] Sara: Our SLA for discharge pipeline is 500ms p95, so we need to keep latency tight.
[02:33] Jordan: Right — smart routing could help: route short notes to high-precision pool with autoscale, longer notes to quantized pool.
[02:40] Tom: Do you support that routing today?
[02:42] Priya: Yes, Redwood's routing policy can split by route or request metadata. We can set a rule based on note_length or a tag from your ingestion step. Default fallback if high-precision unavailable goes to quantized model.
[02:55] Evan (Meadowline Security): Quick sec question — earlier you shared SOC2 and encryption docs. Did you confirm KMS/HSM support?
[03:03] Jordan: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations; the private deployment (Redwood Private) can use dedicated HSM in VPC. I'll re-send the KMS diagram.
[03:12] Evan: Thanks — also need logs retention details for audit.
[03:15] Alex: We shared the audit log doc in the folder — Jordan will reshare with Evan annotated.
[03:19] Priya: Back to quality — we recommended two immediate mitigations: make the concision constraint conditional for inputs <100 tokens, and add a short "preserve medications/allergies" line in the prompt. We validated on a 400-sample subset and recovered ~3 of the 4 Rouge-L points for the short-note bucket.
[03:37] Maya: Did that change introduce any regressions elsewhere?
[03:40] Priya: Minimal. The triage precision dipped 0.7% — within noise. We also ran toxicity/PII checks — no increase.
[03:47] Tom: Sounds promising. What's your confidence at scale?
[03:50] Priya: We want to run a 3k-sample regression across the full dev+prod-ish sample to be confident; that will catch edge cases.
[03:58] Jordan: That's one of the action items. Priya, can you run that on the q4 quantized variant and the non-quantized baseline so we can compare?
[04:05] Priya: Yes — I'll run both. We'll upload a spreadsheet with per-prompt scores, diff flags, and example failures.
[04:11] Sara: On scoring — can you remind us of the rubric you're using?
[04:14] Priya: Sure. It's a mixed metric: entity recall (weighted 0.5 for meds/allergies/procedures), semantic similarity (ROUGE-L/embedding sim 0.3), and human-rated correctness 0.2. We also flag hallucinations separately. The scoring sheet includes thresholds per class.
[04:29] Maya: The human-rated piece — how often are humans in the loop during POC?
[04:33] Jordan: Right now it's spot-checks via your team — we can also set up Redwood's eval tool to collect crowd ratings but for clinical you'll want internal reviewers.
[04:41] Maya: OK we'll handle human review.
[04:44] Tom: Any concerns about guardrails causing false negatives — removing important recommendations?
[04:48] Priya: That was the main tradeoff we saw with the concision guardrail. A better approach is explicit instructions plus conditional logic. Also, if you want stricter safety on triage we can add a secondary classifier that checks for missing meds and reroutes for full-precision rewrite.
[05:03] Jordan: That classifier would add extra cost but could be limited to a tiny fraction of traffic.
[05:07] Sara: Fine if it's targeted.
[05:09] Evan: From security perspective, any new routing or classifier needs to be in the audit scope and use same KMS/keys.
[05:16] Jordan: Absolutely. All deployed components will inherit your KMS and audit logs under the Private plan.
[05:21] Priya: Also small note — during last week's A/B the templating we used had a typo: referenced "Redwood Dedicate" in notes, so some docs showed that misspelling. Not related to model perf but FYI.
[05:33] (laughter)
[05:35] Maya: Nice.
[05:36] Priya: Sorry, that was my slide.
[05:38] Jordan: Next up — fine-grained guardrails. We demoed a prototype auto-fallback in the playground. Any feedback?
[05:45] Tom: We liked the idea — the manual rollout controls look useful. Can you include a way for us to pin model-version per route in the UI?
[05:52] Priya: Yes — the console supports per-route model pins and rollout percentages. We'll show you a short walkthrough next week.
[05:58] Sara: On timeline — if the 3k regression looks good, what's typical pilot extension cadence?
[06:03] Jordan: Usually 2 more weeks of regression + live shadow traffic, then a canary roll for the high-precision route. So roughly 3–4 weeks from now.
[06:12] Tom: That works.
[06:13] Jordan: Any blockers on compliance? Evan?
[06:16] Evan: Need to confirm one item around egress controls in the VPC deployment — I'll mark it in the questionnaire. Otherwise looks ok.
[06:23] Jordan: Great. Let's confirm action items then.
[06:26] Priya: I'll run the regression tests and upload results to the shared folder.
[06:30] Jordan: I'll send the updated prompt set with conditional logic and the scoring sheet.
[06:34] Maya: I'll add 50 edge-case prompts from our triage logs.
[06:38] Evan: I'll review SOC2 and the egress item.
[06:41] Jordan: Any other questions?
[06:43] Tom: One quick thing — pricing impact if we route 10% of traffic to non-quantized pool?
[06:48] Jordan: Rough back-of-envelope: if non-quantized is 1.8x cost, routing 10% would be +8% overall token spend. We'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[06:57] Tom: Great.
[06:58] Jordan: OK, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene same time next week — same agenda unless something urgent comes up.
[07:05] Sara: Thanks all.
[07:07] (call ends)
